roleTitle: Fraud Detection Data Scientist, Card Payments
jobDescription: We process card payments for about 9,000 merchants. The Fraud Detection Data Scientist builds and recalibrates the real-time fraud scoring models, designs features from authorisation, merchant and device data, measures model performance with the fraud operations team and documents every model change for the model risk committee. The model risk policy requires a master's or doctoral degree in a quantitative discipline for anyone who signs off model development, and the team is starting work on network features that link cards, devices and merchants.
requirements: Builds and recalibrates fraud scoring models on card authorisation data.
Designs features from authorisation and device data, including network (graph) features linking cards, devices and merchants.
Measures model performance with the fraud operations team, including alert rates and fraud capture.
Documents model changes for a model risk committee.
Holds a master's or doctoral degree in a quantitative discipline.

evidence.text: Data Scientist, Fraud, Quayside Payments (March 2021 to August 2026): recalibrated the card-not-present fraud model every quarter with gradient-boosted trees trained on labelled chargebacks, and compared each recalibration with the live model on a holdout month.
Built velocity features (transactions per card per hour, distinct merchants per device per day) in the feature store and wrote unit tests for their time windows.
Met the fraud operations team weekly to review alert rates, fraud capture by value and analyst workload against the agreed thresholds.
Wrote the model change notes for each recalibration, covering data windows, performance against the incumbent model and known limitations, and presented them to the model risk committee.
Analyst, Westbury Insurance (September 2019 to February 2021): built claims-fraud referral rules in SQL and reported weekly referral volumes to the claims team.

Work sample: an anonymised model change note for one recalibration, with the training and holdout windows, precision at the operating threshold, the effect on alert volumes and the model risk committee's approval minute.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate would need to give two months' notice and has asked whether the role can be based at the Bristol office three days a week.
Education verification: the registrar of the University of Kelsall confirmed in writing that the candidate was awarded an MSc in Operational Research with merit in November 2018.
